findings.reason: entity.mjs:36 now calls decodeHTML, which in entities ^4.4.0 (package.json:49) defaults to legacy mode and decodes semicolon-less prefixes like `&not`. NAMED_RE at line 7 matches all of `¬it;`, so the output differs from match[0] and lines 37-45 consume the whole match as an entity. The baseline's decodeHTMLStrict left it unchanged.
findings.claim: Switching to decodeHTML (legacy mode) decodes unknown named references that start with a legacy entity name (e.g. `¬it;` becomes `¬it;`) instead of leaving them literal as CommonMark requires.
findings.evidence: NAMED_RE (`/^&([a-z][a-z0-9]{1,31});/i`, line 7) matches the whole `¬it;`. With entities ^4.4.0 (package.json:49), `decodeHTML` defaults to DecodingMode.Legacy, which decodes semicolon-less legacy prefixes such as `&not`, `&copy`, `&amp`, `&lt`, so `decodeHTML('¬it;')` returns `¬it;`. That differs from match[0], so lines 37-45 push a text_special token with that content and consume the full match. The baseline's `decodeHTMLStrict` only decoded complete `name;` references, so it returned the input unchanged and the rule fell through to `return false`. The spec says only names on the HTML5 entity list are recognised (test/fixtures/commonmark/spec.txt:714-720).

findings.reason: A grep of test/ for `&(not|copy|amp|lt|gt)[a-z]+;` finds nothing, and the diff adds no tests, so locked tests pass under both decoding modes. Severity lowered to low because this is a coverage gap: the actual defect is the merged C1/X1 item.
findings.claim: No test covers an unknown entity that starts with a legacy prefix, so the suite cannot catch the regression.
findings.evidence: The diff touches only entity.mjs and adds no tests. The existing non-entity fixtures (`&x;`, `&ThisIsNotDefined;`, `&hi?;`, `&MadeUpEntity;` in test/fixtures/commonmark/good.txt:322-348) contain no legacy prefix such as `&not`, `&amp`, `&lt` or `&copy`, so legacy and strict decoding give the same output for all of them. A grep of test/ for `&notit` or `&copy[a-z]` finds nothing.
